summary: The prepared base reproduces the reported AttributeError in the actual Gemma4Unified constructor/inherited-forward path. At the exact candidate commit, the same regression passes for tied and untied embeddings, CPU-AMX materialization/loading, numerical first forward, and ROCm graph capture/replay. Independent GPU numerical and pipeline-parallel constructor checks also pass. The change mirrors the established Gemma4 multimodal tied-head logic and contains no native changes.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before regression: four failures, including the exact missing lm_head_is_tied AttributeError; the GPU graph test alone passed because capture does not reach the assertion that failed earlier tests until construction/forward setup.
Five candidate regression cases: tied and untied construction/first forward, tied CPU-AMX load propagation, untied independent loading, and GPU graph capture/replay with numerical reference.

gpu_execution.evidence: Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 reported cuda_available=True on AMD Instinct MI350X. Candidate regression performed torch.cuda.CUDAGraph capture/replay, and independent tied/untied numerical forwards ran on that GPU.

remaining_limitations: The reported google/gemma-4-12B-it server startup and gated weights were not exercised.
The available architecture was AMD MI350X/ROCm 7.2, not the report's NVIDIA H100/CUDA environment.
Actual multi-process pipeline-parallel execution and a physical CPU AMX host were unavailable; those paths were checked with constructor/loader isolation.

Heavyweight Gemma4 decoder components were substituted in focused tests while retaining the real unified constructor, loader, inherited forward, Transformers Gemma4UnifiedConfig, and GPU graph machinery.
No native source changed, repository-environment.json specifies no native build, and no native rebuild was applicable.
